summary: Good news if you live in Minneapolis: we checked, and Minneapolis is no stricter than Minnesota. Minnesota's regulated-animals law (Minn. Stat. 346.155) covers dangerous exotics like big cats, bears, and primates, not rodents, so a pet rat is unregulated statewide. Minneapolis licenses dogs, cats, and ferrets and regulates dangerous and exotic species and reptiles, but imposes no restriction on keeping a pet rat. A pet roof rat is allowed, the same as Minnesota.

keep.why: Minnesota's regulated-animal statute (Minn. Stat. 346.155) lists dangerous exotic species (large cats, bears, primates, etc.) and does not include rodents, so a pet rat is unregulated at the state level. Minneapolis Title 4 (Animal Care and Control) licenses dogs, cats, and ferrets and regulates dangerous and exotic animals and reptiles, but has no restriction on keeping pet rats. Not stricter than Minnesota.
keep.governing_law: Minneapolis Code Title 4 (Animal Care and Control); Minn. Stat. 346.155 (regulated animals; rodents not listed).

breed.why: No local rodent-breeding restriction; the state's permissive rule applies.

sell_give.why: No local restriction on giving or selling a pet rat; the state's rule applies.

transport.why: No local transport restriction on a pet rat; the state's rule applies.

sources.title: Minneapolis Code of Ordinances Title 4 (Animal Care and Control)
Minnesota Statutes 346.155 (Possessing regulated animals; rodents not listed)
